fact_text: In March 2026 the government announced a fuel price subsidy of roughly Rs 50 to 55 per litre on petrol and diesel, which the analyst estimated at about Rs 2 billion or more per day.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A fuel subsidy that is sustained beyond a short period drains dollar reserves, not just rupees, because petroleum imports are paid in dollars and the country cannot subsidise them indefinitely.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When fuel is underpriced, investors and oil marketing companies hoard imports expecting a price rise, which raises import volumes and dollar cost together, creating a double loss.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In March 2026 the analyst treated the government's fuel pricing, which follows international prices with a lag of up to about two weeks, as the single most important factor for whether the bull market framework holds.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In March 2026 the analyst framed the Middle East conflict as two scenarios, a quick end or a prolonged war; in the prolonged case, energy shortages from Hormuz disruption were expected to be priced in within two to four weeks.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's reasoning favours refineries and oil and gas exploration companies during an oil price spike, since their earnings benefit when crude prices rise.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Prolonged high oil prices make LNG expensive, so power plants shift to coal, which can raise coal demand and prices; companies with oil-linked raw materials or heavy coal input are therefore hurt.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cites 2011 to 2014 as a period when the PSX index rose alongside higher oil prices, while acknowledging there are also periods when oil rose and the index fell.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Whether the index rises or falls with oil depends mainly on its valuation (cheap or expensive) and on current government policy; a normally priced index declines less when oil rises.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In March 2026 the analyst put the PSX index at roughly 6.5 to 7 times earnings, which he read as historically cheap for future returns.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's arithmetic: if average company profits grow about 18% a year, earnings roughly double in four years; if the index P/E also re-rates from about 6.5 to 12-13, the index could rise about fourfold.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst lists oil price doublings in short periods in 1990, 2003, 2007 and 2022 as crisis episodes to check against PSX returns and valuations after the market's correction.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst lists how the government manages the current account deficit as a factor in whether an oil shock hurts the index, since poor management weakens the bull market framework.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In March 2026 the analyst reasoned that subsidies are announced to please voters, and that no election was close enough at that point to force a reversal of the subsidies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'War Time Investing - 16 March 2026' (YouTube transcript, undated)
